login.title: Sign in
login.lead: This is your private tool. Only your own Google or Microsoft account can sign in.

connect.title: Connect your mailboxes
connect.lead: We read sender, subject and list headers to find companies. We don't read your email bodies.
connect.partial: Read access granted. Sending will ask for permission the first time you send.
connect.unverifiedBody: Google will show “Google hasn't verified this app”. That's expected for your own private app. Check that the app name and developer email are yours, then choose Advanced → Go to StopDisturbance.

errors.state: The sign-in link expired. Try again.
errors.missing_read_scope: Read permission is required to scan.
errors.no_refresh_token: The provider didn't return long-term access. Remove the app from your account permissions and connect again.
errors.tenant_not_allowed: Only Outlook.com/Hotmail accounts, or a Microsoft 365 organisation you administer, can be connected.
errors.no_id_token: Microsoft didn't confirm your identity. Try again.
errors.connect_failed: Something went wrong while connecting. Try again.

connect.h1: Find who has your data. Ask them to delete it.
connect.sub: You approve every message before it's sent.
connect.microsoftNote: Microsoft may show that the app is unverified. That's expected for your own private app; check the app name is yours before accepting.
connect.partialRow: We can scan but can't send yet. We'll ask for send permission before your first request.

interstitial.title: Heads up: Google will show a warning
interstitial.body1: This is your own app, so Google hasn't reviewed it. Google will say “Google hasn't verified this app”.

interstitial.revoke: You can remove access at any time at

setup.title: First-run setup
setup.lead: About a minute. You can change all of this later in Settings.
setup.invalid: Please enter your name and pick a country.
setup.name: Your name as companies know you
setup.nameHelp: Used in the letters we draft for you. Companies use it to find your records.
setup.aiRules: Rules only, no AI — nothing is sent to DeepSeek.
setup.aiGate: DeepSeek can be turned on only after you confirm its training opt-out in

consent.do1: Read sender, subject and date of your emails (not the message body).
consent.do2: Send the requests you approve, from your address.
consent.do3: Watch for replies to those requests only (we open the body of those replies, nothing else).
consent.store: Company names, email counts and dates, up to 3 subject lines per company, and the requests you send.
consent.never: Read email bodies to scan, sell your data, or send anything you didn't approve.

ai.title: How we use AI
ai.body: When AI assist is on, the app sends these to DeepSeek using your API key: sender display names, sender domains, up to 3 redacted subject lines per company and header flags (for grouping and tagging), and public privacy-policy text (to find contact addresses). Letters are written from templates on this server; your name, email, message bodies, your other contacts and OAuth tokens are never sent. DeepSeek's own terms decide how they store API data. Switch to “Rules only” to send nothing.

scopes.title: Exactly which permissions & why
scopes.meaning: What it lets the app do

googleProfile.name: Google openid email profile
googleProfile.text: Your name and email address, to create your account.

gmailRead.name: Google gmail.readonly
gmailRead.text: Read your email. We can technically read message bodies, but we don't: the scan reads only sender, subject and date. We open only the replies to requests you sent, to show them to you.

gmailSend.name: Google gmail.send
gmailSend.text: Send the requests you approve, from your own address. Nothing else.

msRead.name: Microsoft Mail.Read
msRead.text: Same as above for Outlook: headers only for the scan; we open only replies to your requests.

msSend.name: Microsoft Mail.Send
msSend.text: Send approved requests from your address.

msOffline.name: Microsoft offline_access
msOffline.text: Keep watching for replies when you're not on the site.

ai.sent: Sender display names · sender domains · up to 3 redacted subject lines per company · header flags · public privacy-policy text.
ai.never: Email bodies · attachments · your name, email or phone · other contacts · OAuth tokens · ID numbers · letters.

whatWeSee.title: What we can see
whatWeSee.lead: This is your own private app. Here is exactly what it reads, keeps and never touches.

read.title: What we read
read.body: For scanning: the sender, subject, date and list headers of your emails. Never message bodies. The only bodies we open are replies to requests you sent, so we can show them to you.

store.title: What we store
store.body: Company names, email counts and dates, up to 3 subject lines per company (deleted 90 days after the scan), your decisions and the requests you send. Mailbox access tokens are encrypted.

never.title: What we never do
never.body: Read email bodies to scan, sell or share your data, or send anything you didn't approve.

ai.title: AI
ai.body: AI assist is off by default (Rules only). If you turn on DeepSeek in Settings, only sender names, domains, up to 3 redacted subjects per company, header flags and public privacy-policy text are sent.

control.title: You stay in control
control.body: Nothing is pre-selected and nothing is sent without your explicit approval. You can disconnect a mailbox or remove the app's access in your Google or Microsoft account at any time.
